prerequisites: Adequate foundation in calculus and algebra

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling learning new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: analyze the situation and problems qualitatively and quantitatively. Formulate hypotheses and solutions using the models typical of industrial engineering.
Work effectively in a group, integrating capacities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of industrial engineering.
Rationally apply energy balances in the main equipment that are part of thermal installations.
Analyze thermal equipment and installations with the tools derived from the Second Law and interpret the results in terms of energy saving and efficiency.
Identify and analyze heat transfer modes and reflect on possible means to increase or reduce the heat transfer rate.
Fluently handle various forms of representation, such as graphs, tables, diagrams, or formulations, both to extract information and to use them when expressing results.

syllabus_topics: Review of thermodynamic concepts studied in previous courses
Mass and energy balances in open systems
Entropy. Principle of Increase of the Entropy of the Universe
Application to cyclic processes of technical interest
teaching_methods: Individual problem solving for computer practices
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 70% from the written exam, 10% from laboratory practices, and 20% from computer practices (EES). A minimum of 40% in the written exam is required to pass the course; otherwise, only the written exam score will be recorded. Renouncing the ordinary call requires non-attendance at the written exam. For the extraordinary call, students take a written exam (70%) and an additional practices test (30%); positive results from practices obtained during the course may be retained.
